posts.author: DrFreeman
posts.body:
General good starting point:
A starting point for new users (V1.2)
I found a great playlist from Microsoft for learning Javascript when I was doing a refresher course.
There was also the
Free Code Camp
. They have a quite a few courses with free certifications that were quite useful:
Responsive Web Design Certification
JavaScript Algorithms and Data Structures Certification
Front End Development Libraries Certification
Quality Assurance Certification
The certifications aren't directly with RPG Maker, but they help. Maybe sometime there will be formal courses and certification with RPG Maker?
These were some of the websites that had helped me get from doing JS in engineering to RPG Maker:
RPG Maker MV Help File
RPG Maker MZ Help File
RPG Maker MZ API Documentation
RPG MAKER MZ Output Formats
DevDocs
: Massive library for reference to frameworks, languages, and libraries
Repl.it
: An online IDE with cloud compiling
When I get to it in my game, I'll consider doing a tutorial on starting how to script in RPG Maker, but
Driftwood Gaming
and
Sum Random Dude
had a playlist on plugins that helped me.

posts.author: DrFreeman
posts.body:
Free course from Harvard course,
CS50's Introduction to Programming with Scratch
.
Scratch is like a programming language that uses visual cues instead of traditional syntax, you can find the free online version from
MIT here
. While RPG Maker MV & MZ uses Javascript as the programming language, it is still good to learn essentials. Additionally, there is a conversion tool to translate Scratch to Javascript call
LeopardJS
. Many translation processes might be imperfect, they can certainly help you closer. I enjoy WASM, a C++ to JS conversion for the web.
